name: Early-Stage Evaluation of Small Language Models (SLMs) for Scientific Knowledge and Reasoning
description: The task challenges participants to design or adapt evaluation benchmarks that better capture early-stage learning progress of Small Language Models (SLMs), particularly in scientific domains, and to differentiate between models trained on scientific knowledge-focused datasets and those trained on general web data.

cr:input.name: Pre-trained SLMs and Benchmarks
cr:input.description: Participants receive pre-trained SLMs (0.5B, 1B, 3B parameters) with intermediate checkpoints (up to 200 billion tokens) and benchmarks in various formats. Benchmarks include MMLU (MCQs with four options), MMLU-var (continuation-based prompts), and SciQ (question-answer pairs with context). Example MMLU question: 'Find the degree for the given field extension Q(sqrt(2), sqrt(3), sqrt(18)) over Q. Options: A. 0, B. 4, C. 2, D. 6. Answer: B (4).'
cr:input.encodingFormat: [FILL IN THE BLANK: dataset format, e.g., text/csv, application/json]
cr:input.contentUrl: [FILL IN THE BLANK: dataset download URL]

cr:output.name: predictions
cr:output.description: The expected output varies by benchmark. For MMLU: the selected answer (A, B, C, or D). For MMLU-var: the continuation with the highest log-probability among candidates. For SciQ: a binary classification label ('Accept' or 'Reject') indicating whether the question requires domain-specific reasoning.

field.name: mmlu_answer
field.description: Selected answer for MMLU questions. Example: 'B'.

field.name: mmlu_var_continuation
field.description: Continuation with the highest log-probability for MMLU-var prompts. Example: 'C1: (3,3), C2: (4,4), C3: (6,6).'

field.name: sciq_label
field.description: Binary classification label for SciQ questions. Example: 'Accept'.

packages: [FILL IN THE BLANK: additional required packages]

cr:evaluation.notes: Total Score is computed as a weighted combination of Signal Quality (SQ), Ranking Consistency (RC), and Compliance Score (CS). Formula: Total Score = 0.4 × ScoreSQ + 0.2 × ScoreRC + 0.4 × ScoreCS. SQ includes Monotonicity Score and Autocorrelation Strength. RC uses Kendall’s Tau coefficient. CS assesses alignment with scientific knowledge domains.
